narrative.intro: Brookhaven Science Associates obligated $830M in federal contracts in FY2026 to date. Brookhaven Science Associates received 2 awards so far, with an average award size of $415M, and obligations are down 0.5% year over year. The Department of Energy is the primary buyer, accounting for $830M of obligations, while the National Aeronautics and Space Administration accounts for $16K. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) is the dominant market at $830M, with a separate related NAICS entry at $16K. Fiscal-year obligations show a multi-year pattern: FY21 $668M, FY22 $951M, FY23 $789M, FY24 $797M, FY25 $834M, and FY26 $830M. These figures are fiscal year to date totals for FY2026 and reflect contract obligations unless noted otherwise in award-value tables.

sections.heading: How concentrated are Brookhaven Science Associates' FY2026 obligations?
sections.body: The Department of Energy is the largest buyer, accounting for $830M of FY2026 obligations. Brookhaven Science Associates recorded 2 awards in FY2026 to date, producing an average award size of $415M. Obligations are down 0.5% year over year, with FY26 at $830M compared with FY25 at $834M.

sections.heading: What are the main markets and buyers for Brookhaven Science Associates?
sections.body: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) is the primary market at $830M. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration is a secondary buyer with $16K in obligations. The two top NAICS-market entries together reflect the same split between the large DOE-funded R&D work and a small NASA-funded R&D piece.
